tasks.short: Approve and supervise a database installation

steps.what: Read the request to install new databases
Draft the plan and the testing steps

loop.input: request fields and the plan template
loop.output: a plan that names product, target and test
loop.check: Product, target and test equal the form
loop.stop: Stop when the test name is blank
loop.why_not_simpler: How to supervise this installation is not a stored paragraph

steps.what: Approve the schedule for this installation
Supervise the installation and the testing
Sign the testing result for these products

tasks.design: A request names the product, the target, and the test that must pass. The administrator approves a window on {CALENDAR} and a plan in {DOCS}. Supervising the installation and the testing stays in the room or at the console. Only a signed result closes the window on {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Install dates lived in mail, so nobody could show which test had been approved.
tasks.enabler_now: The request can carry product, target and test name, which a plan can cite.
tasks.still_hard: Standing over the installation, and judging a failed test, does not move to a job.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator approves the window, supervises the work, and signs the result.

ambition.what: Approve an install window when the test is named, not when a vendor is already on site

tasks.altitude: The plan is shorter to assemble. The supervision and the approval stay with the administrator.

reach.task: Arrive only inside the signed window
reach.learn: Which test must pass before the window closes

evidence.claim: Installing a database is a plan, a window, supervision, and a signed test result. The product name on a request is not approval.
Digest [S28] reports an unattended agent that deleted a production database, so this installation is supervised and is not applied by an agent.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Supplier time on site is not this role's saving.
Input contract: product name, target name, test name, requested window. Producer is the requester. A request with no test name is not scheduled.
Use the calendar and the workflow form before a custom scheduler.
unknowns: Who may supervise when the administrator is absent.
research_questions: How often does the named test fail on the day?

already_counted.description: The administrator still edits the plan

incremental.description: Update the plan template when a new test type is required

approvals.approved_version: install window approved for this product and test

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests lack a test name, so the plan is written by hand and the visit is unchanged. The high case saves plan assembly only. Supervision and the approval are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write standards that protect vulnerable information

steps.what: List the classes of vulnerable information
Draft standards from the current rule

loop.input: class rows and the current rule
loop.output: a draft that cites class id and rule version
loop.check: Every class id equals the extract
loop.stop: Stop a class that has no owner
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a use is allowed is not a fixed sentence

steps.what: Decide the guidelines for software use
Sign the standards and the guidelines
Store the signed standards version

tasks.design: The administrator names the information class and the software use the standard must cover. A draft in {DOCS} may only restate fields from the current signed rule and the class list. The administrator writes the judgement and signs the standards and guidelines. Staff do not follow an unsigned draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standards were copied between documents, so a rule could protect a class that no longer existed.
tasks.enabler_now: The class list and the current rule version can be cited by id.
tasks.still_hard: What is vulnerable here, and what use is allowed, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides the rule and signs the only version staff may follow.

ambition.what: Re-sign a standard when a class changes, not once a year

tasks.altitude: Less time finding the old text. The decision about vulnerable information stays with the administrator.

reach.task: Confirm the class list before the standard is signed

evidence.claim: A standard for software use is a signed rule tied to an information class. Copying last year's text is not a review.
Digest [S16] and [S17] describe a Dutch cyber duty of care in force from 15 August 2026. Whether it binds this firm depends on sector and size, so the standard does not claim the firm is in scope.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A standard may require a log of access to a class. It does not watch named staff.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Owners confirm classes. They do not sign the standard.
Input contract: class id, software use, current rule version, owner. Producer is the class list. A class with no owner is not put into the standard.
Native document approval before a custom register. No model decides the class.
unknowns: Which classes the owners still recognise.
research_questions: How often is a signed standard reopened because a class was wrong?

already_counted.description: The administrator still checks the class extract
The use decision stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Revise the class fields when an owner adds a class

approvals.approved_version: standards signed for these information classes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the class list is stale, so the draft is discarded. The high case assumes clean classes, but every standard is still signed. Legal scope is not treated as settled.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Pull identifiers from the management system
Draft the logical and physical descriptions

loop.input: identifier rows and the description template
loop.check: Every identifier equals the catalog row
loop.stop: Stop an object with no identifier
loop.why_not_simpler: The logical meaning is not a fixed phrase

steps.what: Direct others only from that draft
Sign the descriptions and the identifiers
Code the signed descriptions into the system

tasks.design: The administrator, or a programmer working to a signed note, writes logical and physical descriptions in {DOCS}. Identifiers are checked against the catalog on {DATA_PLATFORM}. The administrator signs the descriptions before anyone codes them into the management system. A scan of the text is not acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Descriptions were coded straight into the system, so a wrong identifier had already been applied.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalog can confirm an identifier before it is written into the system.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the description matches how the data is really used is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs the descriptions and the identifiers. Directing another person does not remove that signature.

ambition.what: Sign a description when the identifiers match, not at the next model review

tasks.altitude: Checking identifiers is shorter. The decision that a description is right stays human, and nothing is coded unsigned.

reach.task: Code only the descriptions the administrator signed

evidence.claim: A logical or physical description is a text plus identifiers. Coding it into the management system is a second step that should wait for a signature.
Digest [S4] says a person must review code a model drafts, including a description script.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in a large share of tests, so a clean draft is not proof the description is right.
Digest [S28] forbids an unattended write into a live database. Coding the description is a signed apply.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. A programmer may type, but the signature is the administrator's.
Input contract: object name, logical name, physical name, identifier, catalog id. Producer is the catalog. An identifier the catalog does not know is not coded.
Use the platform's native description fields before a custom store.
unknowns: Which objects still lack a stable identifier.
research_questions: How often does the catalog reject an identifier the draft proposed?

already_counted.description: The administrator still checks the identifier list
Editing the description stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Update the description template when the catalog adds an identifier field

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes identifiers are missing, so the check rarely helps and the text is written by hand. The high case assumes clean identifiers, but every description is still signed before it is coded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop data models from named elements

steps.what: Collect elements and the procedures that use them
Draft data models from those elements

loop.input: element rows and the model template
loop.output: a model that names only owned elements
loop.check: Every element name equals a row
loop.stop: Leave off an element with no owner
loop.why_not_simpler: How the elements relate is not a fixed diagram

steps.what: Judge whether the models match the uses
Sign the models and the procedures they cite
File the signed models

tasks.design: Element owners list each element, who uses it, and the procedure that creates it. The administrator draws the model in {DOCS} from those rows, not from a blank page. A procedure with no element is left off. The administrator signs the models before anyone builds to them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Models were redrawn from memory, so an element could appear that nobody owned.
tasks.enabler_now: The element list can supply name, owner, use, and procedure id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the model matches the work is still something the administrator must judge.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator accepts or refuses the model. A picture is not approval.
tasks.altitude: Less time chasing element names. The model decision stays with the administrator.

reach.learn: Which elements were left off the signed model

evidence.claim: A data model is a picture of elements and uses. The rows can be assembled. Whether the picture is true is a person's decision.
Digest [S3] says a prompt can fill document fields and can be wrong. The model cites element ids and is signed by the administrator.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. Owners maintain element rows.
Input contract: element name, owner, use, procedure id. Producer is the element owner. An element with no owner is not drawn.
Draw in the document store the firm already uses. No extra modelling product.
unknowns: Which procedures still have no element row.
research_questions: How often does a signed model omit an element the owner later claims?

already_counted.description: The administrator still checks element rows
The model judgement stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Update the model template when an element row gains a field

approvals.approved_version: data models signed for these elements

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes element rows are empty, so the model is drawn by hand as today. The high case assumes clean rows, but the administrator still draws the judgement and signs it. No build work is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator stops retyping install plans, standards and model notes, and spends the week on whether a product may be installed and whether a model is true.
reach: Suppliers receive the signed install window instead of a loose date.
Programmers receive the signed descriptions they must code to.
skills_to_grow: Separate a signed install window from the work of standing next to the install.
Write a standard as a rule with an owner, not as a slogan about vulnerable information.
Keep a data model tied to named elements.
role.ambitious_version: No new database is installed, and no description is coded, without a signed version.
